AI Overview
PayPal's engineering push into agentic commerce, AI-driven fraud detection, and automated dispute resolution has become a cornerstone of its tech strategy. 
PayPal Newsroom
 +1
While you are likely looking for a specific public engineering blog post authored by a team member like "Raj" or "Srini" (potentially referencing Srini Venkatesan, PayPal's Chief Technology Officer), the core of PayPal's 2026 technical disclosures regarding agentic AI spans several major initiatives across their official PayPal Developer Community Blog. 
🧠 1. Agentic Commerce & The Trust Framework
At major industry events like Ai4 2026, PayPal’s CTO Srini Venkatesan emphasized that the primary hurdle for autonomous AI agents making purchases is verifiable trust. 
PayPal Newsroom
The Architecture: In late 2025 and moving into 2026, PayPal rolled out its Agentic Commerce Services (including Store Sync and Agent Ready). These tools allow merchants to export product catalogs into AI environments like Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, and Perplexity. 
www.bankingnewsai.com
Agent Payments Protocol (AP2): To back this up, PayPal co-authored and supported the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) alongside Google. This open extension to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) sets up cryptographic "handshake" mechanisms. It ensures that when an autonomous AI agent executes a transaction on a user’s behalf, the intent is audited, authorized, and safe from "rogue agent" behavior. 
PayPal Developer
 +1
🛡️ 2. Next-Gen Fraud Prevention
PayPal's engineering teams handle massive scale, utilizing their Cosmos.AI platform to deploy large-scale machine learning models. 
Medium
 +1
Network Graph Analytics: To combat sophisticated fraud rings, PayPal’s engineering blog highlights the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and algorithms like node2vec. By linking shared assets (IPs, device fingerprints, and shipping addresses), the system maps fraudulent networks in real time rather than just evaluating isolated accounts. 
H2O.ai
 +2
Real-time Scoring: The AI pipelines analyze over 500 data points per transaction across 400 million accounts, effectively blocking roughly $500 million in fraud per quarter. 
chiefaiofficer.com
⚖️ 3. Automating Fraud Disputes & Claims
A massive shift highlighted in payment engineering discussions is the application of AI to payment reconciliation and dispute workflows. 
Optimus Fintech
80% Reduction in Dispute Times: By leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP) and predictive analytics, PayPal's AI systems ingest unstructured data (such as merchant chat logs, emails, and tracking receipts) to resolve disputes dramatically faster.
Predictive Resolutions: Rather than relying solely on manual operational reviews after a chargeback is filed, the engineering architecture builds an "audit trail" via AI agents. This maps the transaction against a localized knowledge layer to predict if a dispute is fraudulent (e.g., friendly fraud or system abuse) before it escalates to an official claim.
